claude.sample_unit: clinical cases (published case reports; 150 runs across three conditions)

links.outcome: Diagnosis retention under staged versus complete information delivery
links.effect: Under unstructured sequential delivery, models accessed the correct diagnosis in 90% of cases but retained it in only 60%, a 30% Access-Stability Dissociation (Convergence Regression).
links.quote: Under unstructured sequential delivery, models access the correct diagnosis in 90% of cases but retain it in only 60%, creating a 30%  Access-Stability Dissociation invisible under single-shot evaluation.

links.outcome: Gap between vignette-benchmark performance and sequential clinical reasoning behavior
links.effect: LLMs perform well on complete-vignette benchmarks, but under sequential information delivery they abandon correct diagnoses; 90% access vs 60% retention, invisible under single-shot evaluation.
links.quote: Large Language Models achieve impressive accuracy on medical benchmarks that present clinical information as complete vignettes, but their behavior under sequential information delivery, the standard mode of real clinical practice, is poorly characterized.

unlisted_practices: Structured hypothesis-accountability scaffold (SIPS) for sequential clinical reasoning: raised retention (80% access, 80% final accuracy, 0% Convergence Regression) but reduced top-1 accuracy from 60% to 40%
Multi-dimensional reasoning-quality rubric and failure-mode taxonomy as an audit instrument
